newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy growth set to recover after slowdown - Credito.
newsitem.headline: Italy growth set to recover after slowdown - Credito.

text.p: Italian GDP growth is set to recover after a period of slowdown seen between the first quarter of last year and the second quarter of 1996, Credito Italiano said in a report.

"While not being able to talk of a recession in the restrictive sense of the term for the 1995-96 period, it seems more opportune to talk of a slowdown in the economy, with a more marked phase seen in the first half of 1996," the Italian bank said in its latest quarterly report on Italy.

Credito economists said that chart analysis led to the conclusion that "in 1996 and in successive years a recession is not on the cards, if based on the strictest sense of the term as a fall in the level of activity."
Credito forecasts were for growth in Gross Domestic Product of 1.4 percent in 1997.

The bank said it had revised down a previous forecast of 2.2 percent growth due to the impact of the tough 1997 budget which "will weigh on disposable income to the extent of half a percentage point, halving growth in domestic consumption."
But investments and exports will escape the tightening of the economy, it said.
Credito said it also revised down its estimate for average 1997 inflation to 3.0 percent from a previous 3.4 percent "due to costs of imported goods being less than expected."

For GDP growth, the government said it expects to see 0.8 percent this year and 2.0 percent in 1997, but Bank of Italy governor has said next year's growth rate will "not be far from 1996's unsatisfactory figure."
The government has targeted average inflation in 1997 at 2.0 percent and Bank of Italy's Fazio has said a figure of under 3.0 percent was a "realistic target".
